summary: Pin sits on a steep, trackless forested hillside behind the Channel Ten/TX Australia transmission site.
reasons: No track or clearing for a van
Only flat ground is the TV station's own car park

drivers.seclusion: The bush itself is secluded, but it isn't reachable; the only nearby flat ground is the staffed broadcast facility's car park, overlooked by the building.
drivers.access_and_room: No formed track, driveway or gap in the trees leads from the pin to any road; the slope and dense scrub rule out a 2WD van reaching it.
drivers.traffic: Cannot judge traffic on the access road; the car park below serves an operating TV/transmission site, so daytime staff and visitor traffic is likely.
drivers.convention: No sign of anyone parking or camping on the hillside itself; no tracks or tyre marks visible in either image.

flags: Very steep: hillside averages about 21% grade, peaks near 69%, far beyond what a van could sit on
Working broadcast facility (Channel Ten, TX Australia) immediately below means activity and likely cameras/security
sun_shade: Mostly shaded by eucalypt canopy; open grassy patches near the building edge get sun from the north.
cannot_judge: Whether the TV station's car park has after-hours gates or security patrols
Street lighting and night-time activity around the facility
Crossfall or surface of any informal track higher up the slope not visible in these images
